epithet.en: The enslaved narrator who writes his way to freedom
epithet.da: Den slavebundne fortæller, der skriver sig til frihed

1.modern-en: Born in Tuckahoe to an enslaved mother he barely knows and a white father he never names, he witnesses his master whip Aunt Hester until the blood runs—the scene he calls the blood-stained gateway into slavery.
1.modern-da: Født i Tuckahoe af en slavebunden mor, han knap kender, og en hvid far, han aldrig nævner, ser han sin herre piske tante Hester, til blodet løber—den scene, han kalder den blodplettede port ind i slaveriet.

2.modern-en: He spends two childhood years in Captain Anthony's household on Colonel Lloyd's home plantation, where he first hears the slaves' sorrowful songs that teach him slavery's true nature.
2.modern-da: Han tilbringer to barndomsår i kaptajn Anthonys husstand på Colonel Lloyds hovedplantage, hvor han først hører slavernes sørgmodige sange, der lærer ham slaveriets sande væsen.

3.modern-en: Observing Colonel Lloyd's vast wealth, he sees how a slave who honestly tells a stranger his master treats him badly is sold off to a Georgia trader for telling the plain truth.
3.modern-da: Mens han iagttager Colonel Lloyds enorme rigdom, ser han, hvordan en slave, der ærligt fortæller en fremmed, at hans herre behandler ham dårligt, sælges til en handler fra Georgia, fordi han fortalte den enkle sandhed.

4.modern-en: He witnesses the overseer Austin Gore shoot the slave Demby dead in a creek and go entirely unpunished, learning that killing a black person in Talbot County is treated as no crime at all.
4.modern-da: Han er vidne til, at opsynsmanden Austin Gore skyder slaven Demby ihjel i en bæk og slipper helt ustraffet, og han lærer, at det at dræbe en sort person i Talbot County overhovedet ikke behandles som en forbrydelse.

5.modern-en: Chosen above all the other children to be sent to Baltimore, he leaves Colonel Lloyd's plantation with joy and meets his kind new mistress Sophia Auld at the door of Hugh Auld's home.
5.modern-da: Udvalgt frem for alle de andre børn til at blive sendt til Baltimore forlader han Colonel Lloyds plantage med glæde og møder sin venlige nye frue Sophia Auld i døren til Hugh Aulds hjem.

6.modern-en: When Hugh Auld forbids Sophia to teach him further, declaring that learning would unfit a slave for bondage, he grasps that the path from slavery to freedom runs through literacy.
6.modern-da: Da Hugh Auld forbyder Sophia at lære ham mere og erklærer, at lærdom ville gøre en slave uegnet til trældom, fatter han, at vejen fra slaveri til frihed går gennem læsefærdighed.

7.modern-en: Over seven years he teaches himself to read by befriending poor white boys and reading 'The Columbian Orator,' then learns to write by tracing the shipyard carpenters' letters and Master Thomas's copy-books.
7.modern-da: I løbet af syv år lærer han sig selv at læse ved at blive ven med fattige hvide drenge og læse »The Columbian Orator« og lærer derefter at skrive ved at efterligne skibstømrernes bogstaver og Master Thomas' skrivebøger.

8.modern-en: After Captain Anthony's death he is sent back to be valued and divided like livestock among the heirs, falls to Mrs. Lucretia's share, and is returned to Baltimore before Master Thomas takes him to St. Michael's.
8.modern-da: Efter kaptajn Anthonys død sendes han tilbage for at blive vurderet og fordelt som kvæg blandt arvingerne, tilfalder Mrs. Lucretia og sendes tilbage til Baltimore, før Master Thomas tager ham med til St. Michael's.

9.modern-en: Now starved and mistreated by the newly pious Master Thomas, he is hired out for a year to Edward Covey, the notorious slave-breaker, glad at least of the promise of enough to eat.
9.modern-da: Nu udsultet og mishandlet af den nyligt fromme Master Thomas lejes han ud for et år til Edward Covey, den berygtede slaveknækker, glad i det mindste for løftet om nok at spise.

10.modern-en: After six months of brutal whippings nearly break him, he fights Covey for two hours and beats him back, a turning point that rekindles his manhood, then passes a happier year teaching a Sabbath school at William Freeland's.
10.modern-da: Efter at seks måneders brutale piskninger næsten har knækket ham, kæmper han mod Covey i to timer og slår ham tilbage—et vendepunkt, der genantænder hans manddom—og tilbringer derefter et lykkeligere år med at undervise en søndagsskole hos William Freeland.

11.modern-en: He hires out his own time to save money, escapes to New York on the third of September 1838, marries the free woman Anna Murray, settles in New Bedford, and finds his calling reading Garrison's 'Liberator' and speaking at anti-slavery meetings.
11.modern-da: Han lejer sin egen tid ud for at spare op, flygter til New York den tredje september 1838, gifter sig med den frie kvinde Anna Murray, slår sig ned i New Bedford og finder sit kald ved at læse Garrisons »Liberator« og tale ved antislaverimøder.

epithet.en: Frederick's first owner, a cruel and hardened slaveholder
epithet.da: Fredericks første ejer, en grusom og forhærdet slaveholder

1.modern-en: Frederick's first master, he ties Aunt Hester to a joist and whips her bare back bloody, the brutal scene that opens the boy's eyes to slavery's horror.
1.modern-da: Som Fredericks første herre binder han tante Hester til en bjælke og pisker hendes nøgne ryg til blods—den brutale scene, der åbner drengens øjne for slaveriets rædsel.

2.modern-en: As Colonel Lloyd's clerk and superintendent, he oversees the overseers on the home plantation where Frederick spends two years of his childhood.
2.modern-da: Som Colonel Lloyds kontorist og forvalter fører han tilsyn med opsynsmændene på hovedplantagen, hvor Frederick tilbringer to af sine barndomsår.

5.modern-en: He decides to send Frederick away to Baltimore to live with Hugh Auld, the move the boy later regards as the gateway to all his good fortune.
5.modern-da: Han beslutter at sende Frederick til Baltimore for at bo hos Hugh Auld—det skridt, drengen senere betragter som porten til al sin lykke.

8.modern-en: He dies suddenly without a will, forcing his property and slaves—Frederick among them—to be appraised and divided between his heirs.
8.modern-da: Han dør pludseligt uden testamente, hvilket tvinger hans ejendom og slaver—Frederick iblandt dem—til at blive vurderet og delt mellem hans arvinger.

epithet.en: The immensely rich master of the great plantation
epithet.da: Den umådeligt rige herre over den store plantage

2.modern-en: Owner of the great home plantation and hundreds of slaves, he keeps the seat of government for more than twenty farms, where unmanageable slaves are whipped and sold off as a warning.
2.modern-da: Som ejer af den store hovedplantage og hundredvis af slaver holder han regeringssædet for mere end tyve gårde, hvor uregerlige slaver piskes og sælges som en advarsel.

3.modern-en: His fabulous wealth, prized garden, and fine horses come at a savage cost, as when he makes old Barney kneel bareheaded to take thirty lashes over the care of a horse.
3.modern-da: Hans sagnomspundne rigdom, beundrede have og fine heste har en grusom pris, som da han får gamle Barney til at knæle barhovedet og tage tredive piskeslag for plejen af en hest.

4.modern-en: He accepts overseer Gore's defense for murdering the slave Demby and keeps him on, while another of his slaves is shot dead by Beal Bondly for straying after oysters.
4.modern-da: Han accepterer opsynsmanden Gores forsvar for mordet på slaven Demby og beholder ham, mens en anden af hans slaver skydes ihjel af Beal Bondly for at være kommet på afveje efter østers.

5.modern-en: On his plantation Frederick passes his hungry, half-naked childhood, helping Master Daniel Lloyd find his shot birds before being sent away to Baltimore.
5.modern-da: På hans plantage tilbringer Frederick sin sultne, halvnøgne barndom og hjælper Master Daniel Lloyd med at finde hans nedskudte fugle, før han sendes til Baltimore.

epithet.en: The aunt whose brutal whipping he is forced to witness
epithet.da: Den tante, hvis brutale piskning han tvinges til at overvære

1.modern-en: Caught in the company of Lloyd's Ned against her master's orders, she is stripped, tied to a hook, and whipped bloody by Captain Anthony while the terrified child Frederick watches from a closet.
1.modern-da: Grebet i selskab med Lloyds Ned imod sin herres ordre bliver hun afklædt, bundet til en krog og pisket til blods af Captain Anthony, mens det skrækslagne barn Frederick ser på fra et skab.

epithet.en: The cold, ambitious overseer who murders Demby
epithet.da: Den kolde, ambitiøse opsynsmand, der myrder Demby

4.modern-en: The proud, unyielding overseer of the home plantation, he shoots the slave Demby dead in a creek for refusing to come out, then escapes all punishment by calling it a necessary example.
4.modern-da: Som den stolte, ubøjelige opsynsmand på hovedplantagen skyder han slaven Demby ihjel i en bæk, fordi han nægter at komme op, og undslipper derpå al straf ved at kalde det et nødvendigt eksempel.

epithet.en: The Baltimore master who forbids his learning to read
epithet.da: Baltimore-herren, der forbyder ham at lære at læse

5.modern-en: Frederick's new Baltimore master, he and his wife Sophia meet the boy at their door with their little son Thomas, whom Frederick is to look after.
5.modern-da: Som Fredericks nye Baltimore-herre møder han og hans hustru Sophia drengen i døren med deres lille søn Thomas, som Frederick skal passe.

6.modern-en: He discovers Sophia teaching the boy his letters and forbids it, warning that learning would forever unfit a slave for bondage—words that reveal to Frederick the very road to freedom.
6.modern-da: Han opdager Sophia lære drengen hans bogstaver og forbyder det og advarer om, at lærdom for evigt ville gøre en slave uegnet til trældom—ord, der afslører selve vejen til frihed for Frederick.

7.modern-en: In his household for about seven years, his bitter opposition to Frederick's reading only sharpens the boy's determination to teach himself by every trick he can.
7.modern-da: I hans husstand i omkring syv år skærper hans bitre modstand mod Fredericks læsning kun drengens beslutsomhed om at lære sig selv ved enhver kneb, han kan finde.

8.modern-en: After the estate is divided, Frederick falls to Mrs. Lucretia and is sent back to his Baltimore home until a quarrel between Hugh and his brother Thomas tears the boy away to St. Michael's.
8.modern-da: Efter at boet er delt, tilfalder Frederick Mrs. Lucretia og sendes tilbage til sit Baltimore-hjem, indtil et skænderi mellem Hugh og hans bror Thomas river drengen bort til St. Michael's.

11.modern-en: He grants Frederick the privilege of hiring his own time but revokes it in anger over a missed payment, and on every Saturday night demands every cent of the wages Frederick has earned.
11.modern-da: Han giver Frederick det privilegium at leje sin egen tid ud, men trækker det tilbage i vrede over en udeblevet betaling, og hver lørdag aften kræver han hver eneste øre af den løn, Frederick har tjent.

epithet.en: The kind mistress whom slavery corrupts into cruelty
epithet.da: Den venlige frue, som slaveriet fordærver til grusomhed

5.modern-en: Frederick's new mistress greets him with the kindest face he has ever seen on a white person, a sight that lights his arrival in Baltimore with the glow of happiness.
5.modern-da: Fredericks nye frue hilser ham med det venligste ansigt, han nogensinde har set hos en hvid person—et syn, der oplyser hans ankomst til Baltimore med lykkens skær.

6.modern-en: Having begun kindly to teach Frederick the alphabet, she is stopped by her husband, and the deadly poison of unchecked power soon begins turning her angelic face into a demon's.
6.modern-da: Efter venligt at have begyndt at lære Frederick alfabetet stoppes hun af sin mand, og den dødelige gift fra ukontrolleret magt begynder snart at forvandle hendes engleansigt til en dæmons.

7.modern-en: Slavery strips away her tender heart entirely, until she grows even fiercer than her husband and flies at Frederick in a rage whenever she catches him with a newspaper.
7.modern-da: Slaveriet river hendes ømme hjerte helt bort, indtil hun bliver endnu mere rasende end sin mand og farer mod Frederick i vrede, hver gang hun griber ham med en avis.

epithet.en: The mean master whose religious conversion makes him crueler
epithet.da: Den gerrige herre, hvis religiøse omvendelse gør ham grusommere

8.modern-en: After marrying Rowena Hamilton and quarreling with his brother Hugh, he takes Frederick away from Baltimore to live with him at St. Michael's.
8.modern-da: Efter at have giftet sig med Rowena Hamilton og skændtes med sin bror Hugh tager han Frederick væk fra Baltimore for at bo hos ham i St. Michael's.

9.modern-en: A mean man who starves his slaves, he experiences religion at a camp-meeting yet only grows crueler, quoting Scripture to justify whipping the helpless burned woman Henny.
9.modern-da: Som en gerrig mand, der udsulter sine slaver, oplever han religion ved et lejrmøde, men bliver kun grusommere og citerer Skriften for at retfærdiggøre at piske den hjælpeløse forbrændte kvinde Henny.

10.modern-en: When the bloodied Frederick walks seven miles to beg his protection from Covey, he laughs off the danger and orders the boy straight back to the slave-breaker.
10.modern-da: Da den blodige Frederick går syv mil for at trygle om hans beskyttelse mod Covey, ler han faren bort og beordrer drengen direkte tilbage til slaveknækkeren.

11.modern-en: Coming to Baltimore to buy his spring goods, he flatly refuses Frederick's request to hire his own time, warning that it is just another scheme for escape.
11.modern-da: Da han kommer til Baltimore for at købe sine forårsvarer, afviser han blankt Fredericks anmodning om at leje sin egen tid ud og advarer om, at det blot er endnu et flugtforsøg.

epithet.en: The sly, pious slave-breaker who tries to crush his spirit
epithet.da: Den listige, fromme slaveknækker, der prøver at knuse hans ånd

9.modern-en: A poor farm-renter with a high reputation for breaking young slaves, he is hired Frederick for a year so that the boy may be broken to obedience.
9.modern-da: Som en fattig gårdforpagter med et højt ry for at knække unge slaver lejes Frederick til ham for et år, så drengen kan knækkes til lydighed.

10.modern-en: After six months of whippings nearly break Frederick, he is seized by the throat and fought to a standstill over nearly two hours, and never lays an angry finger on the boy again.
10.modern-da: Efter at seks måneders piskninger næsten har knækket Frederick, gribes han om struben og kæmpes til stilstand over næsten to timer og lægger aldrig igen en vred finger på drengen.

epithet.en: The comparatively fair master, best he had until freedom
epithet.da: Den forholdsvis retfærdige herre, den bedste han havde indtil friheden

10.modern-en: An educated gentleman who makes no profession of religion, he gives Frederick enough food and time and works him only between sunrise and sunset, the best master Frederick has until he becomes his own.
10.modern-da: Som en dannet gentleman, der ikke bekender sig til nogen religion, giver han Frederick mad og tid nok og lader ham kun arbejde mellem solopgang og solnedgang—den bedste herre, Frederick har, indtil han bliver sin egen.

epithet.en: The free woman who comes north to marry him
epithet.da: Den frie kvinde, der rejser nordpå for at gifte sig med ham

11.modern-en: His free intended wife, she comes to New York at his summons soon after his escape, marries him before Rev. Pennington, and travels with him to begin their free life in New Bedford.
11.modern-da: Som hans frie tilkommende hustru kommer hun til New York på hans bud kort efter hans flugt, gifter sig med ham hos pastor Pennington og rejser med ham for at begynde deres frie liv i New Bedford.

epithet.en: The abolitionist whose paper and cause ignite his calling
epithet.da: Abolitionisten, hvis avis og sag antænder hans kald

11.modern-en: Through his abolitionist paper the 'Liberator,' which becomes Frederick's food and drink, his cause sets the young man's soul on fire and draws him into the anti-slavery movement.
11.modern-da: Gennem hans abolitionistiske avis »Liberator«, der bliver Fredericks mad og drikke, sætter hans sag den unge mands sjæl i brand og drager ham ind i antislaveribevægelsen.
